historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 guidance midpoint (+7.4%, raised Aug-2026), used as the year-1 base growth. Equity CAGR rejected: the H1-2026 $1.39B leveraged buyback cut book equity from $1,731M to $571M, so book-value compounding describes a capital structure that no longer exists. The 14-19% revenue CAGRs are pre-deceleration history (FY2025 +9%, FY2026 guide +7-8%).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 21.4% is within 30% of revenue (19.5%) and EPS (26.7%), so no formal divergence -- but the equity series ends at FY2025 and is broken by the H1-2026 recapitalisation; it must not be used as a forward proxy.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs use the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - net-share-settlement taxes; interest income not deducted, see inputs). Owner FCF by year: FY2020 -19.8 (SBC+taxes $152.9M exceeded reported FCF $133.1M), FY2021 35.6, FY2022 132.3, FY2023 148.7, FY2024 342.2 (distorted: Q1-2024 reversal of the CEO's 2020 performance award made SBC -$22.9M), FY2025 244.8. The 5-year owner-FCF CAGR is undefined (negative start). On 3 years owner FCF grew faster than reported FCF (22.8% vs 20.6%) only because equity-award taxes fell from the FY2020-21 spike ($62.8M/$65.6M) to $5-45M; SBC itself was 6.9% of revenue in FY2022 and 5.8% in FY2025, then 2.9% in H1-2026. Equity CAGRs were computed FY2020->FY2025 and FY2022->FY2025 on year-end book value.

scenario_narratives.base: Paycom delivers the raised FY2026 guide (+7.5% revenue, ~46% adjusted EBITDA margin) and then settles into a maturing mid-market HCM franchise: growth steps down roughly half a point a year to 3% by FY2035 as the SMB new-logo pool thins and upmarket wins only offset churn, while Beti/IWant automation lifts the adjusted margin to 47%. Owner FCF margin runs ~22-24% after SBC and equity-award taxes (5% of revenue easing to 4%), 25% cash tax, capex near D&A at 8.5%, and deferred contract costs absorbing half of each year's revenue increase. The Gordon value at 9%/3% binds below the 20x cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: IWant command-driven AI becomes a genuine pricing and win-rate lever and the sales pods expanded from 8 to 10 reps ramp into FY2027-28, re-accelerating bookings so revenue grows 9-9.5% in FY2027-29 before fading to 3.5%; enterprise (1,000+ employee) wins broaden the base and retention climbs above 91%. Automation takes adjusted EBITDA margin to 50% by year 6. The axes are the same as the base case -- bookings re-acceleration and margin -- pushed to the favourable end; nothing here requires float income to rise.
scenario_narratives.bear: The two things the Analysis flags as high-severity land together: US small-business hiring softens (per-employee billings and new logos both weaken) and the Fed eases 150-200bp, stripping $40-50M of near-100%-margin float revenue. Cloud-native rivals discount in the SMB core and the upmarket push stalls against ADP/Workday/Dayforce, so revenue growth fades to 2% by FY2029 and adjusted margin falls back to 42%. With $900M of term debt now on the balance sheet the equity carries that downside with leverage; terminal growth 2% and a 15x cap. The scenario does not approach the zero floor -- the business remains solidly cash-generative.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on a strict house basis: SBC and net-share-settlement taxes expensed, share count held flat at the post-recap fully diluted 45.1M, cash taxes ramped to a normal 25% rather than the FY2025 Section-174 trough, capex and D&A near parity, and deferred contract costs charged as a working-capital drag on growth. Anchored to the raised FY2026 guide rather than either the weak FY2025 cash year or the flattering H1-2026 half. The H1-2026 $1.39B leveraged buyback is treated as a completed transaction: it is in the divisor and in net debt, not in the flows.
key_risks_to_valuation: SBC run-rate: forward SBC incl. taxes is set at 5% of revenue against an H1-2026 run-rate of 4.4% and a FY2025 actual of 8.0%; if the FY2025 level (not H1-2026) is the norm, base IV falls roughly $20/share.

Working-capital drag: wc_capture of -50% of the revenue change is inferred from the OCF residual, not from a disclosed deferred-contract-cost roll-forward (the XBRL tags are absent); +/-20pp moves base IV by roughly $8-10/share.
Float income: ~3% of revenue earns a near-100% margin and moves ~$25.7M per 100bp of short rates; a deeper easing cycle than the bear case assumes would compress margins further.
Leverage: $900M of term debt was added in H1-2026 to fund buybacks; the model deducts it as net debt but does not model refinancing or covenant risk, which would matter only in a bear-case recession.
Terminal value share: ten-year horizon with growth fading to 3% leaves the Gordon value a large share of EV; the WACC x g sensitivity grid shows the exposure.
Share count: 45.14M is the 2026-07-28 cover-page count plus 0.07M dilution; any Q3-2026 repurchases (the authorisation remained open) would lower it further and raise per-share values.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API regular close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 104.90-244.98.
data_sources.financials: PAYC_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL companyfacts, FY2011-FY2025 plus Q1/Q2/H1-2026) for revenue, EBITDA, OCF, capex, SBC, equity; SEC XBRL companyfacts CIK 1590955 fetched 2026-10-02 for the Q2-2026 10-Q anchors (LongTermDebtNoncurrent $900.0M, CashAndCashEquivalentsAtCarryingValue $198.0M, dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding 45,071,619 at 2026-07-28, diluted vs basic weighted shares, PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation, PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock, IncomeTaxesPaidNet, DeferredIncomeTaxExpenseBenefit, pretax income).
data_sources.qualitative: PAYC_Analysis.json (2026-10-02): business model, moat, risks, FY2026 guidance as raised at Q2-2026 results (Aug-2026), bull/bear points.

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 45,071,619 shares on the Q2-2026 10-Q cover page (as of 2026-07-28) plus 0.07M dilutive securities from the Q2-2026 EPS table (45.905M diluted vs 45.836M basic weighted average). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; charging both would double-count. The count fell from 56.1M at FY2025 to ~45.1M after the H1-2026 $1,389.7M repurchase (Q1 $1,054.3M, Q2 $335.4M) -- that is a completed buyback, already in the divisor, not a projected one.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement (SEC XBRL ShareBasedCompensation $118.7M add-back) plus PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation $44.5M in financing. Paycom's adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation adds back only the non-cash SBC line and publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed. H1-2026: $31.6M + $16.6M = $48.2M (4.4% of revenue) versus 8.0% for FY2025.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing outflow $325.5M. H1-2026 repurchases were $1,389.7M, funded by $900M of new term debt plus $172M of cash -- a leveraged recapitalisation that took the count from 56.1M to ~45.1M and the balance sheet from $370M net cash to $702M net debt. The flat-count convention is therefore fully funded (and then some) by actual buybacks; buybacks are value-neutral in this model.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-01T20:00:02Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API; 52-week range 104.90-244.98)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD rate. 10-year UST ~4.1%, ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.05 (mature US SaaS with SMB-cycle and rate sensitivity) gives cost of equity ~9.4%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.7% (Q2-2026 interest expense $10.5M annualised on $900M term debt), ~3.5% after tax. Debt/value ~6% at the current price gives WACC ~9.0%. One WACC across all three scenarios; risk is carried in the driver paths and the probability weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases are immaterial (Paycom owns its Oklahoma City campus and data centres); lease cost stays inside EBITDA, lease liabilities excluded from net debt. One treatment, applied consistently.
inputs.client_funds_note: Funds held for clients (~$3.7B+) and the matching client fund obligations are both excluded from net debt: they are client money in transit, not corporate cash. The interest Paycom earns on that float (~3% of revenue) is operating revenue for a payroll processor and stays in the flows; its rate sensitivity (~$25.7M per 100bp per the 10-K) is modelled through the bear-case margin path.
inputs.interest_income_note: Corporate interest income (part of ~$52M FY2025 other income, net) is NOT stripped: the EBITDA path is built from operating income (op. income + D&A + SBC), which already excludes other income, and the $370M of cash that earned it was spent on the H1-2026 buyback. The company is now net debt, so the net-cash double-count the deduction guards against cannot arise.
inputs.cash_tax_note: FY2025 cash taxes paid $78.1M on pretax $619.4M (12.6%) because deferred tax expense was $154.1M of the $166.0M GAAP charge -- Section 174 / OBBBA domestic R&D expensing catch-up, not a repeatable base. H1-2026 GAAP effective rate 29.3%. The cash tax rate ramps 24% -> 25% (21% federal + state, net of R&D credits), below the GAAP 27-29% that includes non-deductible executive compensation.
inputs.working_capital_note: Paycom capitalises sales commissions and implementation costs (deferred contract costs, ~$1B on balance sheet, amortised over ~10 years). On a cash-tax basis the OCF residual after NI, D&A and SBC ran -$85M to -$115M a year over FY2022-25, 27-60% of each year's revenue increase (FY2025's -$157M also carried ~$66M of tax prepayment timing). Growth consumes cash, so wc_capture_pct is -50 (% of the YoY revenue change). As growth decelerates the drag shrinks with it, which is the right dynamic for a maturing bookings pool.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (operating SaaS/HCM company; routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 1; no prior valuation or memory entry). US-dollar filer and quote, so owner-fcf-adaptations.md does not apply. Fresh build 2026-10-02. FY0 is FY2025 (31-Dec year end); the balance-sheet anchors are Q2-2026 (2026-06-30) because the H1-2026 leveraged buyback moved net debt by $1.07B and the share count by 20%, so FY2025 anchors would be wrong by ~$30/share. Year-1 (FY2026) revenue +7.5% vs the raised guide of $2,197-2,212M (+7.4% midpoint, H1 ran +8.8%); year-1 adjusted EBITDA margin 46.0% = the $1,007-1,022M guide midpoint on that revenue. Projected year-1 owner-FCF margin ~22% sits between FY2025's 11.9% (elevated 13.2% capex, 8.0% SBC+taxes, WC drag) and H1-2026's 29.4% (5.0% capex, positive WC): a deliberately conservative anchor that carries none of the H1 tailwinds forward. Ten-year horizon so growth can decelerate from 7.5% to 3% before the terminal value is taken. info.json carries no fiscal_year_end (the context pack printed 'FY end ?'); it is 31 December.

bear.narrative: SMB employment softens and a Fed easing cycle takes 150-200bp off float yields (~$40-50M of near-100%-margin revenue), while Rippling/Paylocity/Gusto price-compete in the core base and ADP/Workday/Dayforce hold the upmarket. Growth fades to 2% by year 4; adjusted EBITDA margin gives back the FY2026 gains to 42%; SBC held at 5.5% to retain talent; terminal growth 2% and a 15x cap for a low-growth, higher-leverage processor.

base.narrative: Guide delivered: FY2026 +7.5% / 46% adjusted EBITDA margin, then growth decelerates ~0.5pp a year to 3% as the SMB new-logo pool matures and upmarket wins offset SMB churn. Margin drifts to 47% as Beti/IWant automation trims service cost; SBC incl. taxes 5% of revenue easing to 4%; capex ~8.5% roughly matching D&A; cash tax 25%; deferred contract costs absorb half of each year's revenue increase.

bull.narrative: IWant monetises and the expanded sales pods ramp: bookings re-accelerate to high-single/low-double-digit growth in FY2027-29, upmarket (1,000+ employee) wins land, retention climbs back above 91%. Automation pushes adjusted EBITDA margin to 50% by year 6. Same SBC, tax and working-capital mechanics as base; slightly higher capex to fund the enterprise push.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Shifted from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25%: the two high-severity risks in the Analysis (SMB employment cycle, structural growth deceleration) are macro-driven and plausible in a Fed easing cycle that also hits float income directly, and the H1-2026 leveraged buyback means equity now carries that downside with $700M of net debt. Bull cut to 25%: re-acceleration needs IWant monetisation, new-rep productivity and upmarket wins to land together, and consensus (~65% Hold) is explicitly sceptical. Base 50%: the raised FY2026 guide is the most recent and best-evidenced path.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
